object_entity.description: The Acts of Thomas (3rd c.) narrates Thomas's journey to India; the Thomas Christian tradition in Malabar claims apostolic origin; certainty is claimed_tradition.

context_place.notes: Malabar coast of southwest India; traditional site of the Thomas Christians; Pantaenus reportedly found Christians using Matthew's Gospel here (Eusebius HE 5.10).

evidence.notes: Acts of Thomas is the primary source for Thomas's Indian mission tradition.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: The Hymn of the Pearl tells of a prince sent to Egypt to retrieve a pearl guarded by a serpent; he forgets his mission until a letter reminds him; he seizes the pearl and returns to his father's kingdom, receiving his glorious robe; widely read as an allegory of the soul's descent and return.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: We learned the plan of salvation from those through whom the Gospel came to us. Matthew issued a written Gospel among the Hebrews while Peter and Paul were preaching at Rome. Mark, the disciple and interpreter of Peter, handed down what Peter had preached. Luke, Paul's companion, recorded his Gospel. Afterwards John, who leaned on the Lord's breast, published his Gospel during his residence at Ephesus.
